message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Compute Engine VM with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
I’ll give you two ways to do it:

| Method | What you run | Where you run it |
|--------|--------------|------------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your terminal (or Cloud Shell) |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/...` | Any HTTP client (curl, Postman, etc.) |

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You need a service account key or OAuth token with the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` scope.  
> * The **NVIDIA GPU driver** must be installed on the instance after boot (the image we use does not ship drivers).  

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables – change these to your own values
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: install GPU drivers
  --tags="http-server,https-server" \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
```

### Optional: `startup.sh` to install GPU drivers

Create a file named `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver (Ubuntu 20.04)
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
sudo reboot
```

> The `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` line tells Compute Engine to run this script at first boot, installing the driver and rebooting.

---

## 2️⃣ REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the API directly (e.g., from a script or Postman), here’s the exact request body you’d POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT}`, `{ZONE}`, and `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` with your actual project ID, zone, and OAuth bearer token.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Project & billing enabled |
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | GPU‑capable zone selected |
| ✅ | `nvidia-tesla-a6000` accelerator type available in that zone |
| ✅ | Ubuntu 20.04 image family (`ubuntu-2004-lts`) |
| ✅ | Proper scopes (`cloud-platform`) |
| ✅ | (Optional) Startup script to install GPU drivers |

Once the instance is up, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu@<EXTERNAL_IP>
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed. Happy GPU computing!
